deck-238.strengths: Two well-mapped analogies (hotel safe plus concierge for hybrid; offline maps with 'test drive before the trip'), a connected on-device boundary diagram and an estimate-labeled capacity chain.
deck-238.weaknesses: Many label titles, '30% sites without Wi-Fi' and an unhedged 'works where Wi-Fi is restricted' overstate the brief, the 2x2 highlights the cloud quadrant and inverts the sensitivity axis, and the 'traffic jam' and 'specialized team' analogies are throwaways.

deck-277.strengths: Vivid, accurately mapped analogies (in-flight downloads; hotel safe plus concierge), a clear two-lane chevron diagram and a capacity chain explicitly labeled as an estimate to validate.
deck-277.weaknesses: A sparse hero slide, back-to-back analogy slides in the same template, and a tokens/sec slide that is slightly too technical for exec sponsors.

deck-502.strengths: The sensitivity x repetition 2x2 is a useful decision aid for which lane to use.
deck-502.weaknesses: Label titles, an unhedged 'Works offline' claim, fabricated memory allocations (processing 40 GB, headroom 38 GB), a bar chart mixing consultants, summaries and hours, and a weak two-card ask.

deck-900.strengths: Storyline titles turn guardrails into credibility ('Device Speed Is Not Task Success', 'Capacity Worth Measuring, Not Promising'), the boundary diagram is rich and the ask is sponsor-ready ('not a rollout or a promised capacity gain').
deck-900.weaknesses: The portable-office analogy is mostly literal, and the speed chart features a coder model that is irrelevant to consultant drafting.

deck-315.strengths: Made-on-device hook up front, a measured dense-vs-MoE explanation, and shop-floor analogies (shop machines, in-house shop vs outside foundry) tuned to a manufacturer.
deck-315.weaknesses: Two consecutive MoE slides are redundant, one bar chart mixes single-stream and aggregate tokens/s, and the IP problem only appears late.

deck-646.strengths: Strong 'Local By Default, Cloud By Policy' architecture with an approval gate and 'no sensitive IP' label, guardrail-aware memory and throughput titles, and a reviewed-draft developer loop.
deck-646.weaknesses: Opens on hardware rather than the IP problem, the band hub diagram is decorative, the architecture labels are tiny, and the analogies are stock (workshop, librarian).

deck-748.strengths: Touches all required topics, including the made-on-device element.
deck-748.weaknesses: Says 'VRAM and RAM are separate' (car trunk vs cabin), equates tokens/s with words typed per second, labels 28 models as '28 GiB', uses label titles throughout and ends with a vague 'Ready to test local AI?' ask.

deck-977.strengths: Opens with the sensitive-IP problem, weaves in many apt analogies (map zoom, specialist team, open-book exam, shop machines, make-or-buy), uses a like-for-like single-stream chart and ends on a measured self-proof slide (0 cloud calls, 302 s, 9,044 tokens, 3.6 Wh).
deck-977.weaknesses: The routing diagram puts 'Cloud Reasoning' inside the device boundary with no link to the cloud lane, the 'no cloud calls' title subtitle conflicts with hybrid routing, and several titles are labels.
